subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should this Telegram/ACP false-completion class stay open as a core source-turn invariant, or should the remaining claim-verification behavior be treated as plugin/ClawHub scope now that the generic claim-verification proposal was closed?
rationale: Current source has partial delivery warnings and useful plugin hooks, but a core default would affect privacy, compatibility, direct-chat delivery, and plugin API boundaries; automation should not choose that product contract.

options.title: Define a narrow core invariant
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers specify when Telegram/ACP visible success text must be revised, suppressed, warned, or backed by tool evidence.

options.title: Route claim verification to plugins
options.body: Close this direction once maintainers confirm existing hooks plus any small missing correlation seam are sufficient for a ClawHub plugin/package.

options.title: Fold into broader response gates
options.body: Close or mark this as covered by the broader response-gate or human-channel verified-delivery design threads if those become the canonical core policy items.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow core invariant
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers specify when Telegram/ACP visible success text must be revised, suppressed, warned, or backed by tool evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice depends on the product boundary already exercised in the related claim-verification close and source-reply policy reviews.
